Decentralized DNS is Here! No More Censorship!
Handshake moves the DNS ROOT's ownership to the people, instead of controlled by ICANN. This means that a central authority can no longer cease your domain name.

DNS is the system that translates a URL into an IP address. For example voat.co currently resolves to 104.20.81.63. DNS is ultimately controlled by ICANN who mantain the root DNS servers. ICANN was controlled by the US and subject to the first amendment, but Obongo gave up control of ICANN. There are many DNS providers out there, most people end up using their ISP's DNS servers because they don't know any better. The problem with this is the ISP knows your IP and is able to see all of your DNS requests letting them know where you're going on the internet. The other problem with this is the DNS providers can remove or modify DNS entries. For example, if they didn't like voat.co they could redirect it to reddit.

From what I can tell Handshake Naming System (HNS) is a decentralized block chain based DNS replacement to help mitigate the issues mentioned above.
What are the downsides (real, and theoretical) to HNS?

I don't know enough about it to say if there are any significant downsides to HNS, but they're currently importing the top 100,000 domains which means if you're using HNS for obscure URLs it might not resolve them. Also, I'm guessing it probably resolves slower than standard DNS.

Appologies if this is a dumb question:

Could we not get around all of this by just typing in the ip address in the url bar?

It depends on the site, but typically yes. You'll probably run into issues if the site uses host headders (actually pays attention to the URL the user is requesting). You could also put an entry into your hosts file if you know the IP.
